name: Horodok
summary: A Ruthenian town associated with the death of Wladyslaw II Jagiello in 1434.
overview: Horodok, in the Ruthenian lands of the Polish-Lithuanian world, is associated with the death of Wladyslaw II Jagiello.
Jagiello died there in 1434 after a reign that joined Polish kingship with Lithuanian dynastic power.
knownFor: Ruthenian lands of the Polish-Lithuanian world

contentSections.title: Overview
paragraphs: Horodok belonged to the eastern lands connected to the Jagiellonian monarchy and the multiethnic Polish-Lithuanian political world.

contentSections.title: Medieval historical context
paragraphs: Wladyslaw II Jagiello died at Horodok in 1434. His death transferred rule to his young son Wladyslaw III and left the Jagiellonian settlement to be managed by nobles and royal advisers.

contentSections.title: Legacy
paragraphs: The town matters here because it marks the end of the ruler whose conversion, marriage, and victory at Grunwald reshaped eastern Europe.
